body.text: UKPNP International Conference on Jammu Kashmir in House of Commons UK — 8th July 2025

London, 8 July 2025 — The United Kashmir People's National Party (UKPNP) held a landmark International Kashmir Conference in the Boothroyd Room of the Houses of Parliament, London, under the theme: 'Kashmir Conflict: Peace, Security and Fundamental Rights in Jammu and Kashmir'. The conference saw extensive participation from Members of the British Parliament, international human rights activists, legal experts, academics, Kashmiri and oppressed nations' leaders, media professionals, and diaspora representatives.

body.caption: Panel discussion during the UKPNP International Kashmir Conference

body.text: Chief Guest and Keynote Speaker

Sardar Shaukat Ali Kashmiri, Exiled Chairman of UKPNP and Administrative Director of CIRAC to the United Nations, was the chief guest and keynote speaker. In his address, he thanked Members of Parliament for hosting the conference and reaffirmed UKPNP’s commitment to peace, democracy, and human rights.
From the outset, UKPNP has championed secularism, peace, democracy, and reunification of the historical State of Jammu and Kashmir.

He condemned human rights violations and demanded accountability. He also called for the release of political prisoners and emphasized that the future of Jammu and Kashmir must be decided by its people through peaceful and democratic means.
Kashmir is not a territorial dispute between India and Pakistan. It is a matter of life, identity, and dignity for millions of Kashmiris.

body.caption: Conference proceedings at the House of Commons

body.text: Conference Host and Distinguished MPs
Members of the British Parliament highlighted that Kashmir remains one of the longest unresolved conflicts and stressed that its resolution must reflect the will of the people.
Resolutions Adopted
The conference adopted several resolutions addressing human rights, peace, and accountability in Jammu and Kashmir.
Speakers emphasized the need for international engagement, protection of civil liberties, and access for human rights observers.
Condemnation of Extremism
The conference condemned all forms of extremism and violence and stressed that no part of Jammu and Kashmir should be used for proxy conflicts.
Reunification and Future
Reunification of the historical State of Jammu and Kashmir was highlighted as essential for sustainable peace and regional stability.
Concluding Position

Jammu and Kashmir is not a territorial or bilateral issue between India and Pakistan. It is an international issue. United Nations resolutions on Kashmir remain relevant and take precedence over bilateral agreements.
The entire State of Jammu and Kashmir constitutes one historical and political entity and remains disputed. India and Pakistan have no legal right to unilaterally determine its status.
The people of Jammu and Kashmir deserve the right to free movement, reunification, and self-determination in accordance with international law.
